In the Crow way of life, the importance of a large family is often emphasized. This, together with the fact that there is no observable commitment to family planning on the Crow Reservation, led to the use of 1970 fertility rates and to an assumption that these rates would remain constant through the entire period covered under this statement. It must be kept in mind, however, that these rates are high, and if the attitudes of the Crow people change, substantial reduction would be possible. Such a reduction would not significantly affect the size of the Crow labor force until after the year 2000, but it could cause the Crow population to be substantially smaller in the year 2000 than is projected in this study under the assumption of constant fertility rates.
Survival rates were obtained in much the same manner as the fertility rates. Average annual deaths by age, sex, and race were computed for the period 1969-1971. These averages were divided by the U.S. Census population figures for each age-sex group to produce mortality rates for each group. These rates are assumed to remain constant throughout the simulation period.
